How Pricing Works

Four compact steps build your commercial planning estimate.

Start with the operation and a typical goods program, then add ownership, one familiar sizing detail, and your service ZIP. Your price, service rhythm, finish, and return plan stay together in one planning view.

Who owns the goods in this program?

Compare ownership options
Processing-only model

Customer-owned goods

You provide and own the circulating inventory. Shelton handles the recurring pickup, cleaning, finishing, packaging, and return service.

You manage
Initial purchasing, stocking levels, replacement decisions, and any owner-specific standards.
Shelton manages
Scheduled route service, professional processing, finishing, packaging, and return.
Usually fits
Operations with usable inventory already in place or goods that must remain customer-owned.
Full inventory program

Shelton-supplied goods

Shelton helps specify and supply the working inventory, then plans the circulating stock, route service, laundering, finishing, and normal replacement needs as one program.

Shelton plans
Item specifications, starting quantities, circulating backup, route cadence, processing, and the replacement approach.
You confirm
Material and quality level, color, branding needs, usage patterns, storage limits, and presentation standards.
What shapes price
The goods selected, working par, expected loss and wear, finishing requirements, weekly volume, and service frequency.
Usually fits
New programs, inconsistent or aging stock, and teams that want inventory planning handled with the laundry service.

The planning range is an early guide. Exact inventory quantities, replacement terms, and item specifications are confirmed in the account review.

Side-by-side review

Not sure yet

Shelton will compare

03 | Scale & weekly volume

Weekly volume determines the scale of your laundry program.

Share the number you know best, such as pounds, pieces, rooms, or another familiar measure. Shelton uses your selected goods to estimate weekly volume and plan the right production capacity and pickup schedule.
